newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-DEAD SEA CUT TO HOLD.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-DEAD SEA CUT TO HOLD.

text.p: Carnegie Emerging Markets increased its earnings forecast for Dead Sea Works Ltd after the Israeli company reported higher than expected second quarter profit but downgraded the share to a hold.

"We have justified our long-term buy rating for DSW on the basis that the magnesium project was due to transform the long-term earnings outlook for the company," analyst Stephen Levey said in a report on Thursday.

"Whilst it appears that the engineering problems that the management of Dead Sea Magnesium have encountered have been solved for the time being, we believe that the risks associated with the project have increased and thus downgrade our recommendation to Hold."
Levey said the projoect has proven to be significantly more expensive than the company orginally expected and break-even may only be achieved next year.

"One of the reasons for this increase in cost has been problems with the quality of the magnesium metal that the factory was producing and management have had to spend significant amounts of money to solve this problem. Although mangement are confident that this has now been overcome, it does increase the overall risk to the project as prices that DSW would receive for low quality magnesium could be as low as 10 percent below market prices," the report said.

Nevertheless, Carnegie increased its forecast for net income in 1997 to $47.5 million or $0.166 a share from $41.4 million or $0.145 a share and in 1998 to $55.6 million or $0.195 a share from $52.3 million or $0.183 a share.
